what_was_missing: lib.mjs selfInfo(proc): no longer calls proc.list(). The own start time is computed once per process from its own clock (Date.now() - process.uptime()*1000, written in the 7-digit Z form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffffffZ) and cached process-wide; proc is ignored (signature kept). With proc null the record now also carries this start time instead of null. Removed REAL_SELF_START, the REAL symbol, SELF_CACHE and SELF_NOPROC; realProc.list() no longer stores the own start.

lib.mjs new exports: sameStartTime(a, b) (equal strings match; otherwise both parse as ISO 8601, any number of fractional digits, Z or offset, and lie at most 2000 ms apart; null/unparseable never matches another value) and START_TOLERANCE_MS = 2000. No existing export changed name or signature; no file format changed.

lib.mjs comparisons now use sameStartTime: realProc.alive (PowerShell CreationDate vs the recorded start), killOwnTree (listed child vs recorded child; descendants and the child are re-checked through alive), and sameRecord in the stale-lock break (pid and nonce exact, start time within tolerance). descendants keeps its exact rule (a child never starts before its parent).

Normal path is PowerShell-free: taking a free lock, appendLedger, withRunLock/checkCe, logOrphans and release make no proc call; proc.alive runs only when a lock file is already there (judging its holder). Verified by tests T36c (reader that throws on every call is never called) and T36d (realProc plus a child_process spy: zero subprocesses).

lib.test.mjs: T28 expects the own-clock start (equal to selfInfo(null).start_time, ISO7 form, within 1 s of now minus uptime); T29 expects proc.list called 0 times; T31's fake alive compares with sameStartTime against the own start. Added T36c, T36d, T36e (stale lock of a gone holder broken only after alive answered false, rename after the judgement; with no provider or a throwing alive it stays), T36f (real ended child, broken after one real realProc verification), T85 additions (own-clock start within tolerance of PowerShell's, alive true for it, listed start +1 s alive, -5 s not), T90c (sameStartTime 1 s match, 5 s no match, exactly 2 s match, 2.001 s no, offsets/fraction digits, nulls; killOwnTree 1 s off kills grandchild then child, 6 s off kills nothing).

CONTRACT.md 4.4: own start time from the process's own clock, proc not consulted, no PowerShell on the normal path, two-second tolerance in the stale judgement and the break re-read. 4.9: start_time form instead of exact-string comparison, sameStartTime/START_TOLERANCE_MS described, selfInfo and killOwnTree wording. spec/lib.md: T28, T29, T85 updated; T36c-T36f and T90c added.
Test run through the lane: full lib.test.mjs passed (exit 0, 69.7 s, lane label lib-harden-test); the changed and new tests by name: 12 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped (lane label lib-harden-test-named).
deviations_from_the_spec: selfInfo(null) now returns the own-clock start time rather than null, so a lock taken with no provider (dry modes) records a real start_time; the record format is unchanged.
sameRecord (the break's re-read) applies the two-second tolerance as the brief asked; since the nonce must still be equal, this cannot make a different record count as the one judged stale.
lib_change_requests: status.mjs line 129 and handover.mjs line 130 compare a PowerShell-listed start_time with a recorded one (lock, watcher, alarm records written from selfInfo) by exact string equality: with own-clock start times these never match, so a live holder or watcher would be judged dead. Replace `p.start_time === rec.start_time` with `lib.sameStartTime(p.start_time, rec.start_time)` in both (the owners of those files must make the change).

status.mjs line 627 (`wlock.start_time === watcher.start_time`) and watch.mjs line 683 (`cur.start_time !== self.start_time`) compare two values both taken from the same process's selfInfo, so they still hold; switching them to lib.sameStartTime would be harmless and uniform.

Tests outside lib.test.mjs that build a record for this test process with a PowerShell start (status.test.mjs line 534, psStart(process.pid)) and expect a script to match it against a listing should pass once status.mjs uses sameStartTime; they were not run here.
open_points: Timing BEFORE the change: one real start of render.mjs that takes run.lock (realProc) and appends two ledger lines (labels-missing path, minimal synthetic run root under tcb-build/tmp), measured once through the lane: 2292 ms (lane log, label lib-harden-time-before).
Timing AFTER the change: the same command on the same kind of root, measured once through the lane: 73 ms (lane log, label lib-harden-time-after).

Risk to weigh: the tolerance is symmetric (2 s) as briefed. Node's process.uptime() starts some milliseconds after Windows' CreationDate; on a stalled machine with a below-normal-priority process that gap could exceed 2 s, and then a LIVE holder would be judged dead and its lock broken. A reused pid can only have started AFTER the recorded holder, so an asymmetric rule (match when the reported CreationDate is up to, say, 60 s earlier than the recorded own-clock start, but at most 2 s later) would keep pid-reuse detection and remove that risk. Not implemented because the brief fixes five seconds apart as no match; owner's call.

edgeFacts(flags, proc) still calls proc.boot() (PowerShell) when a caller passes a provider and no --boot; only replace.mjs does so, and only when it needs the boot id. It does not judge another process. Deriving boot from os.uptime() would need the same tolerance wherever a recorded boot is compared; left unchanged.
